t: Microsoft adds outside "workplace and productivity data" companies as a data source, and age checks for logged-out users
x: Microsoft's privacy statement now says it gets data from companies that supply workplace and productivity data for product research, and may use device info to apply age protections when you aren't signed in.

t: Fable 5.2 launches at 20% lower output and caching prices than Fable 5.1
x: Anthropic's pricing page now lists Fable 5.2 at $40 per million output tokens, down from $50 for Fable 5.1, with prompt caching also 20% cheaper. Fable 5.1 moves to the legacy list.

t: Your cash back rate is now "personalized" and may differ from other members'
x: Rakuten's Oct 23 terms and privacy policy say cash back rates are personalized by your account history, shopping behavior and membership status, so your rate at a store may differ from another member's. Cash back is now "Rewards," with partner-point conversions and a $2,000-a-day gift card cap.

t: Dec 1: one account per person, and AI will analyze project content and editing history until you delete the account
x: From Dec 1, Vrew allows only one account per person (no team sharing on one login) and will use AI to analyze project content, assets and editing history for personalization, kept until the account is deleted. Object via chat support by Dec 1.

t: Dec 4 terms: a verified email domain can see your account and public sites, and may absorb the account after notice
x: From Dec 4, an org that verifies your email's domain can see that your Netlify account exists, its plan, and your public sites' names, URLs and last deploy dates. If it also has a Netlify subscription, your account can move under its control unless you change your email in the notice window.

t: Price match will pay wallet credits, not a refund
x: From Dec 10, Booking.com's US price-match promise changes from a refund of the difference to Wallet Credits. They can still lower your reservation price if possible.

t: Inactive accounts kept 5 years, and ad partners can now measure store visits
x: BeReal now waits five years before deleting an unused account, and shares ad IDs with partners that can measure store visits where you agree.

t: Checked bags now $50 to $85 each, and all of December is peak
x: For trips booked from Nov 3, JetBlue's first checked bag costs $50 to $70 and the second $70 to $85. Every day in December now gets the higher peak fees.

t: Wells Fargo's Nov 24 Online Access Agreement: AI agents act as you, and you must prove you revoked them
x: From Nov 24, whatever an AI or automation tool does in your Wells Fargo account counts as you doing it, and you stay responsible until you report revoking it and can show proof.

t: Free accounts: inactivity window doubles from 12 months to 24
x: Proton will now wait 24 months, not 12, before it can delete an unused free account and its Mail, Drive, Calendar and Pass data.

t: Smule's Dec 4 terms: your recordings can train AI and be licensed to other companies, and under-18s are out
x: From Dec 4, Smule may train AI on your recordings and license de-identified copies to other companies to build AI, old songs included. The opt-out only opens Dec 4.

t: PayPal's "false information" rule now spells out what counts: identity, account or business, goods, transaction details
x: PayPal's ban on "false, inaccurate or misleading information" now names identity, account or business, goods or services, and transaction details.

t: Hulu and Disney+ terms: "add-ons" wording dropped, device type added as a reason content can vary, ESPN dispute-notice address changed
x: Disney+/ESPN/Hulu terms now list your device type as a reason content may differ, drop "add-ons" wording, and move ESPN's dispute-notice address.

t: Stripe's Nov 20 privacy rewrite: AI voice agents, your data to your bank, and calls used to train AI
x: Stripe's new privacy policy, effective Nov 20, lets AI voice agents call people and use the recordings to train AI, and says it may send your IP, email, phone and address to your card's bank.

t: Social Security updates its SSN master file: new Treasury 'Do Not Pay' data sharing starts Dec 3
x: SSA's file on everyone issued an SSN adds a routine use letting it share records with Treasury's Do Not Pay system to catch improper payments. Comments close Dec 3.

t: Calm says it may now infer health traits from feelings you share, and adds AI terms
x: Calm's Oct 13 privacy policy drops its promise not to infer health traits from feelings you share in messages. New terms cover AI features fed with your emotions and stress.

t: Tubi moves onto Fox's privacy policy: it can now collect your precise location, and its no-targeted-ads age for teens drops from 18 to 16
x: Tubi's Oct 22 privacy policy is Fox's joint policy: it allows precise location, adds AI tools for ads and support, and cuts a teen targeted-ads limit from under-18 to under-16.

t: Premium free trial back to 1 month as the 2-month offer ends
x: Spotify's two-month free Premium trial ended on schedule. New subscribers now get one free month, then $12.99 a month.

t: Toyota now lists training large language models as a use of your personal information, and adds Acxiom tracking across your devices
x: Toyota's Oct 28 privacy notices add "training large language models" as a use of personal data, including connected-car data, plus Acxiom cross-device tracking and AI in customer support.

t: Claude's $200 plan becomes "Ultra": no 5-hour limit, but 10x Pro's weekly usage instead of 20x per session
x: Claude Max 20x is gone. The $200 plan is now Ultra: no 5-hour limit for verified accounts and 10x Pro's weekly usage. Max is a single $100 plan with 5x.

t: Cash App's saved checkout info now extends to loyalty programs and in-store Square checkout, and the Local Cash tip rule changes
x: Cash App's terms rename "Checkout powered by Cash App" to "Buyer Features," adding loyalty and rewards programs and Square point-of-sale devices. A rule forcing tips onto Local Cash is gone.

t: Canva adds e-signatures, and its new terms say it doesn't verify who signs and isn't an archive for your signed documents
x: Canva's updated Terms of Use (effective Oct 30) point to new e-signature terms: Canva doesn't check signers' identity, bans wills and powers of attorney, and says keep your own copy.

t: Social Security is building one 'Client Data System' profile on everyone with an SSN, combining 12 record systems
x: A new SSA records system keeps one profile per SSN: citizenship, earnings, benefits, marriage history, call notes, alert flags. Email may be used for surveys. Comments close Nov 29.

t: GitHub Enterprise now includes Copilot for every licensed user, with AI usage billed against your budget from the first request
x: GitHub's pricing page now lists "GitHub Copilot access" in the Enterprise plan. There are no per-seat AI credits: Chat, code review and cloud agents draw on the company's AI budget.

t: Grindr's new terms: AI can summarize your chats for other users even if you don't use AI, and opting out won't lower your bill
x: Grindr's new terms say its AI may generate summaries about you from your chats and show them to other users, whether or not you use AI. Turn those settings off and paid features may stop, with no change to your bill.

t: Xero can now require ID and a face scan or cut off your account; US disputes get a 1-year deadline from Dec 28
x: Xero's new terms let it demand a government ID and a biometric face scan, and suspend or close accounts that don't pass. US customers also get new arbitration rules, including a one-year limit on claims.

t: Notion's pricing page stops saying "unlimited" file uploads, listing "Up to 5 GB" on paid plans
x: Notion's pricing table now lists paid-plan file uploads as "Up to 5 GB" instead of "Unlimited", and drops "unlimited" wording from several other rows.

t: 1Password's business terms add paid Professional Services and drop the right to cancel if setup fails
x: 1Password's business subscription terms now cover paid setup and training services. A clause letting customers terminate if 1Password couldn't finish setting up the service was removed.

t: Slack drops "24/7 support" from its plan table; the free support tier now targets a 2-business-day reply
x: Slack's pricing page no longer lists 24/7 support with a 4-hour first response. The free Standard Success Plan targets a 2-business-day case reply; faster help is a paid add-on.

t: From Jan 1, California charges sales tax on software subscriptions, but not on streaming, music, e-books or games
x: Starting January 1, 2027, downloaded and cloud software (SaaS) sold to Californians gets sales tax of 7.25% or more. Streaming, music, audiobooks, e-books and games are excluded.

t: From Dec 1, a 60-day wait before small claims court and no more online dispute notices
x: From Dec 1, Cricket customers must mail a dispute notice and wait 60 days before small claims. You can reject the change by mail within 30 days of Cricket's text.

t: From Nov 1, you must send a notice and wait 60 days before taking AT&T to small claims court
x: From Nov 1, AT&T customers must send a dispute notice and wait 60 days before suing in small claims, and AT&T can make its settlement offer later in arbitration.

t: From Nov 25, companies can choose the only way you're allowed to stop their robocalls and texts
x: From Nov 25, a company can name the only way you're allowed to stop its robocalls and texts, and replying STOP to one kind of alert may not stop the others.

t: Privacy policy now says user data isn't used to train any AI models
x: Todoist's privacy policy now says your data isn't used to train any AI models. It used to rule out only "generalized" ones.

t: Standard plan card now says unused monthly picks don't roll over
x: Audible's Standard plan card now says unused monthly picks don't roll over, a rule that was already in the FAQ.

t: Terms rename the Offline Fee and Off-Platform policies
x: Two Airbnb policies get new names in the terms, the Offline Fee Policy and the Off-Platform Policy. The rules read the same.

t: Third-party apps stop getting your Fitbit data Oct 30 unless you reconnect them in Google Health
x: Apps linked to your Fitbit stop getting new data on Oct 30 unless you reconnect each one through Google Health.

t: Enterprise plan now notes you can connect multiple GitHub organizations
x: Figma's Enterprise plan now notes you can connect multiple GitHub organizations to one plan.

t: Plan cards now list in-person selling features instead of a one-line blurb
x: Shopify's plan cards swap a one-line blurb about in-person selling for a feature list. POS Pro is still $89 a month per location.

t: ipl.org shuts down Nov 9, 2026: logins end, uploads and public pages go offline, nothing is migrated
x: ipl.org goes offline for good on Nov 9. Logins end, uploads and public pages disappear, and nothing moves elsewhere.

t: New Oct 21 terms call customer support "a courtesy," not an obligation, when carriers, banks or sellers are at fault
x: Shein's new terms say helping with problems caused by carriers, banks or marketplace sellers is "a courtesy," not an obligation.

t: "Audio imports" added to motion design features
x: Figma's motion features now include audio imports. Prices didn't change.

t: Tax tools now fall under one Shopify Tax terms document
x: All of Shopify's tax tools now fall under one Shopify Tax terms document. The separate Automated Filing terms are gone.

t: Plan cards rewritten; prices unchanged, Basic's 2% store fee now spelled out
x: Squarespace rewrote its plan cards: Basic's 2% store fee and each plan's AI credits now appear on the cards, and the automated-tax fee line is gone. Prices didn't change.

t: Gift Registry shuts down after Dec 27, 2026, and saved registries will be deleted
x: IKEA's U.S. gift registry closes after Dec 27, and saved registries are deleted, not moved anywhere.

t: Nov 17 terms: report broken purchases to the developer, not Google; Play services now covered
x: From Nov 17, Google Play's terms tell you to report broken purchases to the developer instead of Google, and drop "defective" content as a refund example.

t: Nov 12 terms: mass claims go to one arbitrator, ads follow you to your TV, and a 30-day opt-out
x: From Nov 12, 25 or more similar claims against Pinterest go to one arbitrator, and its ads can follow you to your TV. You get a 30-day window to opt out of arbitration.
Slack lists a new "Frontline teams" add-on for Enterprise+, with no price shown.

t: Premium free trial doubled to 2 months for new users, until November 1
x: New Spotify Premium Individual subscribers get two free months instead of one, until Nov 1. Then it's $12.99 a month.

t: Inactive free accounts: deletion warnings are now only a "courtesy"
x: Proton used to promise warnings before deleting inactive free accounts. Now the warnings are "a mere courtesy" it will "aim" to send.

t: $5 a month in Verizon Dollars if you keep Do Not Sell off and let Glance lock-screen ads track you
x: Verizon will pay up to $5 a month in Verizon Dollars if you let the Glance lock-screen app track you for ads and keep your Do Not Sell settings off.

t: Senders now billed for unpaid foreign duties on packages, even if disputed, with 6% interest
x: If a foreign country says duties weren't paid on your package, USPS can now bill you for them, even if you dispute it or the package is lost, with 6% interest.

t: Two sets of yearly prices for Grow and Advanced are rotating on the pricing page
x: Shopify is showing some visitors $79 and $299 yearly prices and others $89 and $359 for the same plans. It looks like a price test.

t: From Nov 1, Roblox says it is merchant of record for most platform purchases; parents must accept for minors
x: From Nov 1, purchases on Roblox are bought from Roblox itself, not from creators, and players under 18 need a parent to accept the new terms to keep playing.

t: Contract moves to Italian affiliate Dec 1; Brazil users lose local law and get arbitration; no password-manager use
x: On Dec 1 your Evernote contract moves to an Italian company, Brazil users get arbitration, and storing passwords or financial info is banned.

t: Plan comparison adds AI agents and tools, donations, and a rental platform
x: Wix's plan comparison adds rows for AI agents and tools, donations, and a rental platform. Prices didn't change.

t: Bill negotiation moves to $15/month Premium+ on Nov 2
x: From Nov 2, Rocket Money only negotiates bills for $15-a-month Premium+ members. The pay-only-if-it-works option and automatic renegotiations end.

t: App locks Nov 4 unless you accept new arbitration terms
x: Oura's app stops working Nov 4 unless you accept new terms: arbitration with a jury waiver, mass claims handled 20 at a time, and no opt-out.

t: AI secret detection now covers push protection, billed by usage
x: GitHub's AI password detection can now block pushes, but that feature is billed by usage instead of being included in Secret Protection.

t: Gmail, Photos and Drive data you share with Search or Gemini can now shape ads
x: Google's promise not to use Gmail, Drive and Photos content for ads now has an exception: if you let Search or Gemini read that data, it can shape your ads.

t: Terms now let Proton discontinue any service or feature without notice
x: Proton can now change, suspend or shut down any service or feature, with or without notice. It says it will try to warn you but isn't obliged to.

t: Arbitration now covers vendors like Stripe; robot deliveries added
x: DoorDash's arbitration clause now covers its vendors too, like Stripe and Persona. All U.S. cases move to JAMS, and robot deliveries are written in.

t: Auto-enrolls accounts in class-action claims, keeps 20% of payouts
x: Robinhood will file class-action claims for you by default and keep 20% of the payout. In those cases you also lose the right to sue. You can unenroll.

t: Limited-time offer: $99 for a year of Premium
x: A banner offers a year of Audible Premium for $99, about $8.25 a month. The page doesn't say when the offer ends or what its terms are.

t: Data pipeline pricing replaces "free during beta"
x: Cloudflare Pipelines is no longer free during beta. It now has real prices, with monthly free allowances before per-GB charges start.

t: Airline delay-category rule pushed to Feb 1, 2027 (flights from Jan 1)
x: DOT's rule letting airlines stop counting ten kinds of disruptions as their fault now starts Feb 1, 2027, so holiday flights stay under the old categories.

t: Regulatory Charge rises 24% to $0.26 per voice line on Nov 1
x: Verizon's own Regulatory Charge goes from $0.21 to $0.26 per voice line on Nov 1. It's a Verizon fee, not a government tax.

t: Narrows error and fraud protection for linked external-account transactions (Oct 19)
x: If you pay a Bank of America card or loan from an account at another bank, BofA no longer investigates most errors or fraud on those payments. The other bank has to.

t: Annual plans: cancellation now effective next billing cycle
x: Audible's annual Premium plans now say cancellation takes effect at the next billing cycle, not right away.

t: New Figma Specs beta added to paid seats
x: Paid Figma seats now include Figma Specs (beta), and Figma Make gets secrets management and a built-in backend. Prices didn't change.

t: Claude Enterprise now lists a 20-seat minimum
x: Claude Enterprise now requires at least 20 seats, which means at least $4,800 a year before any usage.

t: Enterprise+ now has a public price: $45 per user
x: Slack Enterprise+ used to say "Contact sales." It now shows a price: $45 per user a month, billed annually.

t: Yearly prices up 13% to 20% on Grow and Advanced
x: Paying yearly for Shopify Grow or Advanced now shows $89 or $359 a month instead of $79 or $299. Monthly prices didn't move.

t: AI credits and Basic’s 2% store fee spelled out
x: The pricing page now lists AI credits for each plan and spells out Basic's 2% online-store transaction fee. Prices didn't change.

t: Optional auto-sell of bitcoin to fund ACH debits
x: Cash App can now sell your bitcoin automatically to cover ACH debits, if you turn the feature on. You may not get a notice before each sale.

Services that are ending, and the data that disappears with them.

Companies passing responsibility to someone else.
Small edits to plans and pricing pages.

t: Claude plans and pricing (November 2026): Free, Pro, Max and Ultra compared
x: Short answer: Free costs nothing, Pro is $20 a month (or $17 a month billed annually, $200 up front), Max is $100 a month and Ultra is $200 a month. Ultra replaced the old $200 Max 20x plan in late October 2026. It has no 5-hour limit for verified accounts and 10x Pro's weekly usage.

t: Disney+ price change history (2019–2026): every increase, plus current plans and prices
x: Short answer: as of our November 7, 2026 check, Disney+ costs $12.49 a month with ads and $21.49 a month for Premium (no ads), or $214.99 a year. Both went up on September 23, 2026. Ad-free Disney+ launched at $6.99 in November 2019 and has risen six times since, up about 207%.

t: Does Proton delete inactive accounts? How to keep a free Proton account (2026)
x: Short answer: yes, free ones. Proton can delete a free account inactive for 12 months in a row, with its mail, files, calendar and passwords. Since October 20, 2026, the warning emails are only "a mere courtesy." Logging in once a year keeps the account.

t: How to opt out of Google using Gmail, Photos and Drive data in Search, Gemini and ads
x: Google's privacy policy now lets Gmail, Photos and Drive data shape your ads, but only if you connect those apps to Search or Gemini. Here's how to check, and how to undo it, using Google's own pages.

t: HBO Max plans and prices (November 2026): Basic with Ads, Standard and Premium compared
x: Short answer: HBO Max has three US plans as of our November 5, 2026 check: Basic with Ads at $10.99 a month, Standard at $18.49 and Premium at $22.99. All three went up on October 21, 2025, and Standard has risen three times since HBO Max launched at $14.99 in May 2020.

t: How to opt out of arbitration (2026): opt-out deadlines at Pinterest, Grindr, DoorDash, AT&T and more
x: Short answer: many companies give you 30 or 31 days to opt out of arbitration, usually by email or mail, starting when you sign up or when you're notified of new terms. Some offer none. Here is what each company's terms say, with the dates that matter now.

t: How to stop robotexts and robocalls: the FCC's reply-STOP rule from Nov 25, 2026
x: Short answer: reply with exactly the word the text names (STOP is safest), or use the key-press option on a robocall. From November 25, 2026, a company can make that its only accepted way to opt out, and a STOP to one type of alert may not stop the others.

t: Netflix plans and prices (November 2026): with ads, Standard and Premium compared
x: Short answer: Netflix has three US plans as of our November 3, 2026 check: Standard with ads at $8.99 a month, Standard (ad-free) at $19.99 and Premium at $26.99. Basic is gone. All three went up on March 26, 2026, and Standard has risen eight times since it launched at $7.99 in 2011.

t: Oura arbitration terms (Nov 4, 2026): can you opt out? What you can do before the deadline
x: Short answer: no. Oura's new terms, which you must accept in the app by November 4, have no way to opt out of arbitration. Here is what they do let you do, quoted from the terms.

t: Paramount+ plans and prices (November 2026): Essential vs Premium compared
x: Short answer: when we checked paramountplus.com on November 10, 2026, Paramount+ Essential was $8.99 a month or $89.99 a year, and Premium was $13.99 a month or $139.99 a year. Both monthly plans have gone up three times since 2021, and Paramount's new owner says a Paramount+ and HBO Max bundle is coming in early 2027.

t: Spotify Premium plans and prices (November 2026): Individual, Duo, Family and Student compared
x: Short answer: as of our November 8, 2026 check of spotify.com, Spotify Premium in the US is $12.99 a month for Individual, $18.99 for Duo, $21.99 for Family and $6.99 for Student. All four went up in January 2026, the third US increase since July 2023, after Individual sat at $9.99 for twelve years.

t: Xbox Game Pass plans and prices (November 2026): Ultimate, Premium, Essential and PC Game Pass compared
x: Short answer: when we checked Microsoft's US store on November 9, 2026, Game Pass Ultimate was $22.99 a month, Premium $14.99, Essential $9.99 and PC Game Pass $13.99. Ultimate peaked at $29.99 in October 2025 before Microsoft cut it in April 2026, and from November every console plan includes only a set number of cloud gaming hours a month.
